Vet & Lazy’s first beers were produced in the Summer of 2015 – the company has only scaled um since. Now, Vet & Lazy sells 6 beers in multiple stores such as Alber t Heijn and is becoming famous in the Rotterdam region. To quantify their growth, the brewer started with a production of 30L to the production of 40hl/month but aimed to increase this potential to 100hl/month. Vet & Lazy aims at having a positive societal impact by using local raw materials directly from the producer. As such, intermediaries are cut and the direct link to the producers enables them to receive a fairer price for their product. As such, Vet & Lazy benefits the local community. The brewer also has a positive impact from an environmental perspective. First, since the company mainly uses raw materials from local sources, the ecological impact is reduced since they do not come from far away foreign countries. Second, the company developed multiple technological tools to reduce its CO2 impact. One example of it is a technological initiative to use the production heat to heat the floor of Blue City Rotterdam. Third, as the production of beer uses a lot of water, Vet & Lazy partially uses the water of the Maas river as an incentive not to waste pure water. Fourth, Vet & Lazy will also partner with other organisations to for example use the waste during the beer production and recycle it to transform it into products that can be consumed. Customers: Vet & Lazy targets any beer lover in the B2C market. More recently, however, the company also operated with major B2B retailers such as Albert Heijn. Still, the final target remains beer lovers who appreciate good local beer brewed by a brewer with character. sample_text: 180 Degrees Consulting Project Brief — The 23plusone Collective PROJECT SCOPE - MEMBERS Organizational Background: The 23plusone Collective is a community of professionals inspiring, shaping, and impacting people and organizations through its scientific method. The collective’s goal is to build a community of change makers through connection, positive action, and mutual inspiration. They do this through their network of experts and workshops catered to unleashing the emotional drivers of individuals and organizations. The three driving forces behind the members are: leading from the heart, moving as one, and shaping what’s next. Over the years, they have developed a deck of cards that help people identify what emotional factors motivate them to better create a sustainable and positive future. Project Brief: The 23plusone Collective has established a new strategy with the key goals of increasing thought leadership, visibility, and community. With a limited amount of hours from members, implementing these strategies can be daunting and difficult without clear execution plans. To support them, 180 Degrees Consulting Delft-Rotterdam will perform a number of tasks, including market and target member analysis, as well as compose concrete outreach plans to attract new members and experts. sample_text: 180 Degrees Consulting Project Brief PROJECT SCOPE Organizational Background Organization: SlimBox Services:Slimbox is a Belgian for-profit companywho developed a new machine that enables to createcustomised packages for products that have to be shipped. When packages are shipped with traditionalpackaging methods, one can see there is usually too much air in the package which makes the shippinginefficient. There are more carbon emissions as the package takes more place in transportation thanwhat the product actually needs. This is also inefficient from an economic perspective as companies tendto pay for more space and weight in transport than what the product actually really needs. By proposingtheir machine to companies, Slimbox enables their customers to make savings from an environmentaland economic perspective. Customers:Slimbox targets B2B customers in Europewho send numerous packages. Slimbox also hasambitions in the short-term to penetrate the US market. Contact Persons:- Filip Roose (co-founder) The problem:Slimbox is a young company and tends to struggle with selling its product to customers. One reason forthis is that they lack strong marketing materials to target customers efficiently. One way to counter this isby having a third-party (=180DC) that could develop an impact measurement calculation of their solutionfrom an environmental as well economic perspective compared to a standard solution. This way, Slimboxwill be able to use the economic- and environmental savings computations when using their machine asa new marketing resource. 180 Degrees Consulting Support: How are we approaching the problem? ● Internal analysis:○ Understand the company and its resources○ Get an understanding of how the machine works ● External analysis:○ Make an assessment of what is traditionally proposed on the market○ Assessment of standard economic and environmental costs when using packages that aretoo large.● Impact measurement computation:○ Environmental Impact measurement
